newsitem.title: SPAIN: SPAIN STUDIES SALE OF 2,700 MILITARY PROPERTIES.
newsitem.headline: SPAIN STUDIES SALE OF 2,700 MILITARY PROPERTIES.

text.p: Spain plans to sell 2,700 military properties as part of an armed forces restructuring, Defence Ministry spokesman Jose Luis Gutierrez said on Tuesday.

He said the ministry had contracted British investment house NatWest Capital Markets and accountants Arthur Andersen to assess the available land and military facilities in relation to the market for the most profitable disposal.
"Spain, like many other western countries, is reducing its military holdings as part of the restructuring of the armed forces," Gutierrez said. "There are many units that are already not being used."
He said the cash raised through the sale was not earmarked for defence spending.

Spain's conservative government plans to modernise the armed forces and is phasing out compulsory service to make the military fully professional. It started selling off its military holdings about 10 years ago.
